summary: Defines how content delivery networks that interconnect (CDNI) can advertise where they can serve users and what they are able to deliver, using the ALTO protocol as the carrier. RFC 8008 describes what such advertisements should mean; this document supplies the concrete protocol encoding. It is a standards-track specification.

plainLanguage.summary: Two pizza shops want to share customers. Each needs to tell the other which streets it delivers to and what it can make. This is a standard note format for sharing that list.

questions: how do cdns advertise footprint and capabilities
what is cdni fci over alto
how does alto carry cdni footprints
what is the altopid footprint type
subtitle: How a CDN tells its partner CDNs where it can serve and what it can deliver, carried over the ALTO protocol.

tldr.problem: RFC 8008 defines what a CDN's footprint and capabilities mean when CDNs interconnect, but no protocol existed to transport and update those advertisements between an upstream and a downstream CDN.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 9241 defines a CDNI Advertisement Service on top of ALTO that carries RFC 8008's advertisement objects as JSON, adds an altopid footprint type, a filtered variant, and a way to look up capabilities per footprint through ALTO property maps.
tldr.outcome: An upstream CDN can fetch, filter and receive incremental updates on a downstream CDN's capabilities with footprint restrictions, using one consistent ALTO interaction model. It is a Proposed Standard.

today: RFC 9241 is a Proposed Standard from July 2022, and the metadata lists nothing that obsoletes or updates it. It relies on the ALTO entity property maps defined in RFC 9240.

sections.title: The Missing Transport for CDNI Advertisements
sections.content:
The CDN Interconnection (CDNI) framework (RFC 6707) defines four interfaces for linking content delivery networks. One of them, the Request Routing Interface, lets an upstream CDN (uCDN) ask a downstream CDN (dCDN) whether it is able and willing to accept a delegated content request.

Part of that interface is the Footprint and Capabilities Advertisement interface (FCI). RFC 8008 already specifies the objects that describe a footprint and capabilities, but defines no protocol to move and update them. RFC 9241 supplies one by adding a new ALTO service, the CDNI Advertisement Service, to the ALTO Protocol (RFC 7285). FCI allows both a push from dCDN to uCDN and a pull query from uCDN to dCDN.
sections.plainLanguage: The two shops already agreed what the delivery list should say. What was missing was a standard way to pass the list back and forth, and this document supplies it.

sections.title: FCI Semantics and Why ALTO
sections.content:
The document first reviews RFC 8008 and RFC 8006. Footprints can be IP prefixes, ASNs or country codes, and capabilities include delivery protocol, acquisition protocol, redirection mode, logging and metadata. Capabilities are expressed with footprint restrictions: a uCDN should consider a dCDN only if the request routing source satisfies all the footprint constraints in the advertisement. Because much is settled by contract, the FCI mainly carries changes and updates, so server push and incremental encoding are needed.

The RFC then lists why ALTO is a good fit: it is aimed at the application layer, its maps can be signed for origin protection, it has a RESTful design and extensive error handling, a network map is a natural way to express a footprint, filtered maps allow partial queries, and it supports server-initiated incremental updates (RFC 8895). Entity property maps (RFC 9240) let a dCDN describe content availability or resource availability per footprint.
sections.plainLanguage: The delivery list changes, for example when a street is closed. ALTO already knows how to send small updates, so the shops do not have to resend the whole list.

sections.title: The CDNI Advertisement Resource
sections.content:
The service conveys JSON objects of media type application/alto-cdni+json. The resource is requested with HTTP GET and has no input parameters or capabilities. Its meta field MUST include a vtag. If it depends on other resources, they appear in uses and the response MUST carry dependent-vtags.

The data is a cdni-advertisement object whose single field, capabilities-with-footprints, is an array of BaseAdvertisementObject items from RFC 8008. Each has a capability-type, a capability-value and a list of footprints, and each footprint has a footprint-type and one or more footprint-value strings. An empty array means the dCDN cannot provide any mandatory-to-implement capability for any footprint. If footprints is null, empty or absent, the capability has global coverage: the dCDN can provide it for any request routing source.

The RFC only requires the server to provide the initial FCI payload types of RFC 8008. It also notes that two entries with the same footprints, one for http/1.1 and one for https/1.1, can be merged into a single entry listing both delivery protocols to save space.
sections.plainLanguage: The list says what the shop can make and, for each item, which streets it covers. If no streets are listed, it means every street.

sections.title: Network Map Footprints and Filtered Advertisements
sections.content:
RFC 9241 adds a footprint type called altopid. Its value is a list of PID names from an ALTO network map, so a PID can stand for a group of IPv4 or IPv6 addresses instead of repeating many prefixes. An advertisement that uses altopid footprints depends on a network map. That map's resource ID MUST be in the uses field and its version tag in dependent-vtags.

The Filtered CDNI Advertisement Service avoids fetching the full resource. It uses HTTP POST with application/alto-cdnifilter+json, carrying a cdni-capabilities list of capability-type and capability-value pairs. An empty list asks for the full advertisement. The server returns only the entries matching a requested capability type whose mandatory properties are a superset of the requested ones, and omits capabilities with no footprints.

An invalid request, such as a null capability-type or capability-value, gets an E_INVALID_FIELD_VALUE error. The vtag in the response MUST match the full resource, so one canonical version tag is used however the query is filtered.
sections.plainLanguage: Instead of listing every house, you can say the north side of town. And instead of the whole menu, you can ask only: which streets get pizza with extra cheese?

sections.title: Looking Up Capabilities per Footprint
sections.content:
The reverse question, what can this footprint get, is answered with ALTO property maps from RFC 9240. Each footprint becomes an entity: an ipv4cidr footprint becomes an ipv4 entity, ipv6cidr becomes ipv6, and altopid becomes a pid entity in the network map the advertisement depends on. A single address in an ipv4 entity translates back to a footprint with the longest prefix, such as /32.

Two new entity domain types are registered: asn, whose identifier is the lowercase characters as followed by the decimal AS number without leading zeros, and countrycode, an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code in lowercase. Neither has hierarchy or inheritance.

A new entity property type, cdni-capabilities, holds a JSON array of capability objects. For a footprint it MUST include every capability the defining CDNI Advertisement resource provides whose footprint restrictions cover that footprint. The defining resource MUST be a CDNI Advertisement resource, with media type application/alto-cdni+json. Both the full and the filtered property map can be used, and both support incremental updates.
sections.plainLanguage: This is asking the other way round: pick one street and ask what the shop can make for people there.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The base ALTO security considerations (Section 15 of RFC 7285) fully apply. The RFC names several CDNI-specific risks: an on-path attacker posing as a dCDN's ALTO server could feed a uCDN false footprints and capabilities, a dCDN could understate its coverage to avoid carrying traffic, property maps could expose network location identifiers, and attackers could request large full advertisements or many small filtered property queries to exhaust a server.

Because RFC 8008 requires integrity and authentication, the uCDN MUST be authenticated to the dCDN, which MUST support HTTP Digest Authentication and MAY support TLS mutual authentication. Credentials and method negotiation are out of scope. A dCDN that serves several uCDNs without isolation could leak one's information to another, so it SHOULD isolate advertisement resources per uCDN, for example with URIs derived by hashing company IDs and agreements, and avoid listing all of them in one IRD.
sections.plainLanguage: The shops must be sure they are talking to each other and not to a fake. And each partner should only see its own list, not the lists meant for other partners.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content: RFC 9241 registers two media types, application/alto-cdni+json and application/alto-cdnifilter+json. It adds the altopid footprint type to the CDNI Metadata Footprint Types registry created by RFC 8006. It also adds the asn and countrycode entity domain types and the cdni-capabilities property type to the ALTO registries created by RFC 9240.
sections.plainLanguage: The document registers its new names in the official lists so nobody else uses them for something different.
